---
title: "For the city"
subtitle: "What Adamsville asks of city decision-makers"
---

Adamsville already has several plans, including the 2020 NPU-H master plan. Based on my research, the bigger problems are following through on those plans and hearing from the residents they are meant to serve. I recommend the following steps.

1. Treat the MLK–Fairburn crossroads as a priority project, and use Hollowell/MLK TAD and Neighborhood Reinvestment Initiative funds to attract a full-service fresh-food retailer and to build sidewalks connecting the food center, recreation centers, the Fain building and bus stops.
2. Involve the community in deciding the future of the Fain building, which has been Adamsville's civic center since 1927. Before APS disposes of it, the city should bring together NPU-H, APS, Parks and Recreation and youth organizations to consider community, youth or senior uses.
3. Make it easier for renters and parents to take part, in line with the master plan's own renter-engagement goal. This could include mailed notices and door knocking (both residents suggested these), meetings with childcare or remote options, and outreach through apartment managers and churches.
4. Connect the Utoy Creek study to street-level drainage problems, and give homeowners reliable guidance and repair assistance, especially older owners who want to age in place.
5. Track investor purchases and short-term rental listings in NPU-H, and enforce existing permit rules, so that the NPU and the council office can see displacement pressure early.

## Limits of this study

Both interviewees moved to the area within the last five years, and both are civically engaged women. Long-time elders, renters, youth and business owners are not directly represented; elders' views appear only through archival records and residents' second-hand accounts. Census estimates for Adamsville's core carry wide margins of error. Future research should interview long-time homeowners, apartment residents, and church and school leaders, and review NPU-H meeting minutes.
